chapter: Hite tours, postwar L.A. and the Central Avenue scene
title: Brother's after-hours place
summary: A wartime after-hours spot first frequented by homosexuals that moved when the police wanted payoffs.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: What was the era of Brothers? Same period?
No, Brothers was World War II thing. That was an entirely different set-up.
Was there music there or was this an after-hours place?

No, after-hours spot. His original place was behind one of the storefronts that faced the Club Alabam and walking back there is like going through the catacombs and it was mostly -- it started out being strictly fre-

quented by homosexuals. That's how it started. After a while, it became rather popular and other people that were not homosexuals started to going in and having a good time. Sometimes it was amusement and sometimes it was just to have a good drink. So, after that -- Brother stayed at that particular place for a couple of years or so until the law got hot on him and then he moved to another place and when the police wouldn't stand their payoffs there, then he'd move to another place. Brothers ended up having the same name at two or three different addresses.
